title: Model choice for interactive face generation
prompt: Your app generates face images on demand while the user waits on screen for the result. Faces must look convincing but need not be flawless. Which model architecture should power the generator?
constraint: Users wait interactively for each result, so perceived latency is the priority; image quality must be good but not flawless.

options.why: A GAN produces a face in one forward pass — millisecond-scale generation that keeps the interactive wait short, and modern face GANs (e.g. StyleGAN-class) already clear the 'good but not flawless' bar. It directly satisfies the latency-first constraint, making it the best fit.

A distilled / few-step model cuts the many denoising iterations down to 1-4 steps, so latency is acceptable for an interactive wait and quality is decent. Defensible, but distillation usually trades away some fidelity and still tends to lag a one-pass GAN on raw speed — a weaker fit than the GAN under this constraint.

Full diffusion runs dozens of sequential denoising steps, producing the best fidelity but seconds-long generation. That maximizes quality the constraint says you don't need while wrecking the perceived latency the constraint prioritizes — wrong trade-off here.

Generating a face token-by-token or pixel-by-pixel is inherently sequential and the slowest option at inference. It optimizes nothing the constraint asks for and badly violates the interactive-latency priority.
